title: First system from scratch
sub: A sheet with hit points and armor class, a die, and a “Strike” that hits a target.

sheet.title: Sheet
sheet.sum: The sheet has a “Combat” block: “Hit points” 10, not below 0, and “Armor class” 12.

dieStrike.title: Die and strike
dieStrike.sum: There is a “Check die” d20 and a “Strike” effect on every sheet.

checkDamage.title: Check and damage
checkDamage.sum: “Strike” rolls the die against the target's armor class and on success takes off 5 hit points. No errors, the trial showed it.

alone.title: On your own
alone.sum: You built the effect without hints.

block.lead: A system is the rules of your game. In this lesson we will build a hero with hit points and armor class and a “Strike”: on a hit it takes 5 hit points off the target. The lesson runs on a practice copy — your system does not change.
block.say: Create a “Combat” block on the sheet.
block.open: Above the sheet press “blocks and sheet types”.
block.name: Type the name “Combat” and press Enter.
block.result: The “Combat” block is on the sheet.

hp.say: Add a “Hit points” field to the “Combat” block.
hp.addHint: Can't see the “+ field” button? Click the block name “Combat” — it expands.
hp.name: Type the name “Hit points” and press Enter.

hpStart.say: So that a new hero starts with 10 hit points, open “more” on the “Hit points” field and type 10 into “In a new sheet”.
hpStart.hint: Did the “Hit points” field close? Click “Hit points” in the “Combat” block.
hpStart.result: Hit points: 10 in a new sheet.

hpMin.say: So that hit points do not go negative, in the same place type 0 into “Not below”.
hpMin.hint: “Not below” is a formula field: after you click, typing goes into the formula bar at the top of the screen. Enter or “done” saves.
hpMin.result: Hit points: 10 in a new sheet, not below 0.

ac.say: Add an “Armor class” field to the “Combat” block, 12 in a new sheet.
ac.addHint: Can't see the “+ field” button? Click the block name “Combat”.
ac.name: Type the name “Armor class” and press Enter.
ac.start: Open “more” and type 12 into “In a new sheet”.
ac.startHint: Did the “Armor class” field close? Click “Armor class” in the “Combat” block.
ac.result: Armor class: 12 in a new sheet.

die.say: Create a d20 die for checks.
die.hint: Create the die before the check: a new check takes the first die of the system.
die.add: In the “Rolls” section, under “Dice”, expand “+ die” and choose “one die — d20”.
die.name: Type the name “Check die”. Leave the 20 sides as they are.

strike.lead: An effect is what a hero can do: a strike, healing, a spell. An effect with a button appears for the hero at the table as a button.
strike.name: Type the name “Strike” and press Enter.
strike.result: The “Strike” effect is created. For now it has one input — “Who acts”.

everyone.say: So that every hero has “Strike”, on the “Sheet” tab, in the “What it gives all sheets” section, add “Strike”.
everyone.open: Above the sheet press “blocks and sheet types”.
everyone.all: In “Sheets” press “all blocks”: the section is shown only on it.
everyone.pick: In “What it gives all sheets” choose “Strike”.
everyone.result: The “Strike” button is on every hero.

targets.lead: An effect is like a function: everything it needs arrives through inputs, and every input has a kind. A number is damage or a bonus, yes / no is a flag, a “table row” is a row of a reference table, a “sheet” is one hero, a “list of sheets” is any number of heroes. Who to hit is decided at the table, so “Strike” needs a list input.
targets.say: Add a “Targets” input of the “list of sheets” kind to “Strike”.
targets.kind: In “Name” type “Targets”, in “Kind” choose “list of sheets”.
targets.eachHint: One sheet from the list is called by the “Each” field in the steps — name it “Target”.
targets.result: “Strike” has two inputs: “Who acts” is a sheet, “Targets” is a list of sheets, each of them a “Target”.

each.lead: Now a divider: the steps above it run once, the steps below it run for each target in turn.
each.say: In the “Step” palette press “+ for each in the list”.
each.hint: The divider will take the “Targets” list by itself.
each.result: The “For each of” divider stands with the “Targets” list: everything below runs for each target.

check.lead: A roll and a check are two steps: first someone rolls the die, then the result is compared with a number. Here the number is the target's armor class: rolled at least that — a hit.
check.say: Make a roll and a check: “Check die” against the target's armor class.
check.roll: In the “Step” palette press “+ roll”. A roll appears: “Who acts” rolls “Check die”.
check.check: Now press “+ check”. It will compare this roll with 10.
check.formula: In the “Check” line click the number to the right of the sign: the formula opens as a line at the top, and the number 10 is selected in it.
check.formulaHint: The threshold is what stands to the right of the sign. Don't type field names — choose them in the suggestions when you start typing.
check.type: Start typing “armor” — the number will be replaced — and in the group named after “Target” choose “Armor class”.
check.result: A die roll and a check: the result against the target's armor class.

branch.say: On the check step press “+ by result”. A “success” fork appears: its steps run only on a hit.
branch.hint: Don't take “+ change” from the palette: that step would run on any roll.
branch.trap: “Change” stands without a fork — damage will happen on any roll. Delete it and press “+ by result” on the check.

damage.say: Make damage: on success the target loses 5 hit points.
damage.step: In the “success” branch choose “change” in the “+ step” list.
damage.targetHint: At first “Whose” says “Who acts” — that is the hero himself. A strike needs “Target”.
damage.trapOutside: “Change” stands outside the fork — damage will happen on any roll. Move it into the “success” branch.
damage.trapActor: “Whose” says “Who acts” — the strike wounds the hero himself. Choose “Target”.
damage.trapField: The damage does not go to “Hit points”. In “Which field” choose “Hit points”.
damage.result: On success the target loses {{n}} hit points.

problems.say: Press the “No problems” button in the header (if something is found, it says “Problems” and a number). There should be no errors.
problems.hint: If there is an error, “Open” next to it leads to the place.
problems.result: No problems. To close the list, press the same button again.

trial.say: Check “Strike” with a trial: with the die on “maximum”, the line B · Hit points: 10 → 5 will appear in “What came out”. The trial does not change the system.
trial.result: The trial showed: B loses 5 hit points.

heal.lead: Next the system gets published, the book author creates items, and at the table heroes press “Strike”. The last task comes without hints.
heal.say: Make a “Healing” effect: it adds 3 hit points to whoever acts.
heal.hint: “+ button”, then “+ change”: “Whose” — “Who acts”, “Which field” — “Hit points”, “How” — “add”, “How much” — 3.
heal.goal: the “Healing” effect has a change: the “Hit points” of whoever acts go up by 3, and “Problems” shows no errors.
heal.result: “Healing”: +3 hit points to its own sheet.
